video.title: Boston Celtics Fantasy Preview | Can Jayson Tatum & Paul George DESTROY ADP?

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Boston Celtics for fantasy after the trade that sent Jaylen Brown away and brought in Paul George. He thinks Boston is a better and deeper regular season team with Jayson Tatum healthy and George added. He projects a starting five of Derrick White, Baylor Scheierman, Tatum, George and Neemias Queta. Tatum is a comfortable pick from 6 to 8, and George is his best target, with top 30 to top 40 per game upside at an ADP of 76 to 105. Payton Pritchard is his biggest fade because he will be the third option, and White is too expensive at a Fantrax ADP around 34. He also says back-to-back differences between teams are marginal, value should beat positional need in drafts, and mock drafts should be used to practice flexibility.

rules.text: In drafts, value generally beats positional need. Do not go in with a fixed plan to take a certain position in a certain round.
rules.quote: But as a general rule, value just trumps whatever it is you're looking for

rules.text: Use mock drafts to practice being flexible and trying different paths, not to repeat the same pattern. Muscle memory from mocks can make you panic in a real draft.
rules.quote: Have a mockdraft to be flexible, not to repeat the same pattern

rules.text: Back-to-back counts matter only a little. The gap between the best and worst team is about three back-to-backs over a 25-week season.
rules.quote: between the best backto-back team and the worst is three backto-backs over the course of a season

rules.text: The quality games cutoff should be at least 10 games on a day, and the difference over a season is only about six games.
rules.quote: the cut off for quality games should be at least 10 games played on a day

rules.text: Starting usually means more minutes, so a starting role helps a player's fantasy value.
rules.quote: starting inherently gives you a better run at more minutes

rules.text: Do not lean on stats from when one star was off the court if the roster has since added other high-usage players. That data does not fit the new situation.
rules.quote: none of that data accounts for having Paul George there

rules.text: ADPs tend to just follow what happened last season.
rules.quote: the ADPs just seem to follow on exactly what happened last season

rules.text: Players who play limited games and minutes waste a roster spot in leagues where you must always use the slot. They are easier to hold in stash-friendly formats like weekly lock, roto, or deep leagues with games caps.
rules.quote: in 22 minutes, and that's a bit of a waste of that roster spot

player_notes.text: He came back from a torn Achilles much earlier than expected and finished 19th per game in limited minutes. He played 35 minutes a night in the playoffs.
player_notes.quote: He finished 19th per game in limited minutes. 19th.

player_notes.text: He is ranked 8 on ESPN and Yahoo, with an ADP of 8 on Fantrax. The speaker is comfortable taking him anywhere from pick 6 to 8 and calls him good value.
player_notes.quote: I'm very comfortable taking Tatum at number six.

player_notes.text: His only concern is the mystery absence from playoff Game 7, which was called knee soreness. He rates the risk at about 1% and wants to hear at media day that Tatum is fine.
player_notes.quote: in the game seven of the playoffs where he mysteriously didn't play and they were calling it knee soreness

player_notes.text: He does not expect Tatum to play limited minutes or sit back-to-backs.
player_notes.quote: I'm not believing that he's playing limited minutes or sitting back to backs.

player_notes.text: He disappointed people last season because their expectations were too high. He finished 39th in categories and 50th in points leagues.
player_notes.quote: He ended up 39th and 50th in points.

player_notes.text: He is an excellent steals and blocks player. His shooting was bad last season but could and should improve.
player_notes.quote: an excellent steals and blocks guy, but that exact level that he did last season might be hard to keep up

player_notes.text: His usage will likely drop because he moves from the second option to the third behind Tatum and George.
player_notes.quote: So he moves from two to three which is a step down clearly.

player_notes.text: The speaker values him at 40 to 50 in category leagues and outside the top 50 in points leagues. His Fantrax ADP of about 34 to 35 is too early, which makes him a bust at that price.
player_notes.quote: if you're on fan tracks and you see his ad at 35, you don't do it. It's too early.
player_notes.value_hint: 40-50 in cats; too early at Fantrax ADP 34-35; ESPN rank 17 makes no sense

player_notes.text: He was not great last season but still finished 54th per game in category leagues and 65th in points leagues.
player_notes.quote: he was still 54th per game in category leagues and 65th in points less.

player_notes.text: Last season he came in off knee surgery and served a 25-game PED suspension. This season he has had no surgery and comes in fully rested.
player_notes.quote: He entered last season coming off knee surgery. He does not enter this season coming off knee surgery.

player_notes.text: He has an ongoing injury history, including UCL, shoulder and knee problems.
player_notes.quote: Are there some ongoing problems with his arms? He's had UCL problems, shoulder

player_notes.text: He moves from the third offensive option to the second. The speaker would not be shocked by a top 30 per game finish and calls his ADPs (ESPN 105, Fantrax 76, Yahoo 80) too low.
player_notes.quote: I would not be shocked if Paul George ends up a top 30 player per game this season.
player_notes.value_hint: ESPN ADP 105, Fantrax 76, Yahoo 80; top 30 per game upside

player_notes.text: The speaker would happily draft him in the 60s and sees top 40 to top 30 potential if he reaches about 60 games. He is the speaker's best target on the team.
player_notes.quote: I'll happily take him in the 60s. I think this is top 40, top 30 sort of potential.

player_notes.text: The speaker projects about 19 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 1.7 steals, 3 threes, 44% FG and 84% FT in 32 minutes. That would make him a top 40 per game player, and 34 minutes with 23 points would make him top 20.
player_notes.quote: I've got about 196 and four, 1.7 steals, three triples, 44 and 84.

player_notes.text: His game is very fantasy friendly.
player_notes.quote: What if he averages 23 points? That's top 20. His game is very fantasy friendly.

player_notes.text: Boston's 16 back-to-backs are a risk to the case for George. The speaker expects him to sit some of them, maybe 8 to 10, but not all.
player_notes.quote: I'm not convinced that George will sit every one of them though. Maybe 10, maybe eight

player_notes.text: The starting center job is between Queta and Mitchell Robinson. The speaker projects Queta to start, which could take him from 24 to 25 minutes up to 26 to 27, and expects him to close a lot of games.
player_notes.quote: starting maybe makes him go from a 24 to 25 minute player to 267

player_notes.text: He was excellent last season, finishing 112th in categories and 117th in points leagues. The speaker values him at 90 to 110. Push toward 90 if you need a center, and let him slide to 110 if you do not.
player_notes.quote: I think he's pretty solid in this backend zone between 90 and 110.

player_notes.text: He lacks shooting and does not take threes. The speaker says it is slightly possible he starts, but he does not need threes to have value.
player_notes.quote: Does he start taking threes? I'm not going to rule that out completely.

player_notes.text: If Pritchard starts, he would be the third usage player behind Tatum and George. A 29-minute bench role may suit him better than a 32-minute starting role. The speaker projects him as the sixth man.
player_notes.quote: maybe it is better for him to play a 29minute bench roll versus a 32-minute starting role

player_notes.text: If Paul George only plays about 30 games, Pritchard would step back into last season's bigger role.
player_notes.quote: Paul George might play 30 games. True. And then Pritchard will have to step up

player_notes.text: He is the speaker's biggest fade. Last season had perfect conditions for a breakout and he finished only 91st in points and 102nd in categories. His ADP of 74 on Yahoo and 80 on Fantrax is too early, and the speaker will have him on zero teams.
player_notes.quote: He's ranked 74th on Yahoo. He's going at 80 on fan track.

player_notes.text: His minutes are limited by his ankles and foul trouble, and he cannot play back-to-backs.
player_notes.quote: Robinson's going to be limited in minutes because of his ankles, foul trouble

player_notes.text: He gives field goal percentage, rebounds and blocks, though his blocks dropped off.
player_notes.quote: Field goals, rebounds, blocks, but the blocks dropped off.

player_notes.text: He was not a top 150 player in either format last season. The speaker would not spend a draft pick on him at his Yahoo ADP of 108 (ESPN rank 115). He is a category-league streamer, but check his back-to-backs first.
player_notes.quote: He was not a top 150 player in either format last season.

player_notes.text: He is a good stash in stash-friendly formats because he might start or Queta might get hurt. He may only play 55 to 60 games at about 22 minutes.
player_notes.quote: Mitch Robinson's a pretty good stash because maybe he starts, maybe Kada gets hurt

player_notes.text: The speaker expects him to sit every back-to-back.
player_notes.quote: I think Mitch Robinson will sit every one of them.

player_notes.text: He has a chance to start. But he finished 278th in points leagues and 282nd in categories last season, so the speaker calls his Yahoo ADP of 102 and ESPN rank of 167 ridiculous.
player_notes.quote: That Yahoo ADP again is ridiculous at 102.
player_notes.value_hint: Yahoo ADP 102 ridiculous; deep league only

player_notes.quote: ton of threes, but realistically that's that's about it

player_notes.text: The speaker projects him to start, though he is only about 45% sure. He expects only about 20 to 22 minutes.
player_notes.quote: Now I'm only like 45% sure on this, but I think they'll start

player_notes.text: He can shoot and pass, is not a terrible defender, and is bigger than Pritchard.
player_notes.quote: Shyman who's got shooting ability, passing ability. He's not a terrible defender

player_notes.text: He is a late swing pick for deeper leagues. Last season he finished 343rd in categories and 372nd in points. His Yahoo rank is 249, and the speaker has him barely inside the top 300.
player_notes.quote: 343rd for categories, 372 for points leagues. He's ranked this season is 249 on Yahoo.

player_notes.text: In his last 8 games as a starter, at 23 minutes a night, he averaged 10 points, 2.5 threes, 3 rebounds and 2.5 assists. He did not miss a free throw and shot 47% from the field. He is a name to watch in year three.
player_notes.quote: He averaged 10 points, hit two and a half threes, three rebounds, two and a half assists

player_notes.text: He can play the backup point guard role, which may mean Boston does not need Pritchard as a bench ball handler. The speaker has him as the 10th man in the rotation.
player_notes.quote: maybe they don't need that this season because Mike Connley can play the backup point guard role

player_notes.text: Boston picked him up after he was waived. He may take the open two-way slot, but the speaker does not think he is very good or will have a real impact.
player_notes.quote: I don't think he's very good and I don't think he's going to have any sort of real impact
